item.title: By: carl
item.dc:creator: carl
item.description:
<blockquote>Impartiality is the same kind of practice? Using awareness to catch yourself leaning towards something, shirking away from something else and returning to center</blockquote>
Yes, that's it exactly! The Taoist view sees reality as a dynamic ebb and flow, not a static 'perfection' (or imperfection) that we innately tend to get so hung up on.

item.title: By: Lynn Cornish
item.dc:creator: Lynn Cornish
item.description:
Just a thought: In practicing physical balance standing on one foot at the gym, I learned that it is a process of tiny adjustments, being aware of all the little muscles and tissue in your foot and leg, being totally in each moment.
Perhaps impartiality is the same kind of practice? Using awareness to catch yourself leaning towards something, shirking away from something else and returning to center (whatever that is).
It's not that "I am balanced" and will be that way like a statue forever. And so maybe it's not "I am a completely impartial person forever" either.
